q: In LLM chat, what does the "context window" refer to?
options: The monitoring range of a camera
The amount of conversation the model can "remember" and process at once
The size of a phone screen
How many books were used in training
explain: The window is the maximum number of tokens the model can process in one pass; earlier content beyond the window is either truncated or patched by external memory — which is why it "forgets" in long conversations.

q: When AI confidently invents facts that don't exist, the industry calls it "hallucination". What is the main cause?
options: Random errors programmers left in on purpose
Network packet loss
A model is essentially "predicting the next word" — it generates the text that most looks like an answer instead of looking anything up
The user's question is too short
explain: A large model is a probability generator, not a database: it optimizes for "sounds right", not "is true". Asking it for sources on important facts is the only self-defense.

q: In 2026, roughly what does it cost to generate 1 million output tokens (about a full novel) with a mainstream Chinese LLM API?
options: A few CNY to around one hundred
Over ten thousand CNY
Completely free, unlimited
Per-call billing at 1M tokens each
explain: Flagship output prices cluster around 10–100 CNY per million tokens (GLM-5.3 is 28, Kimi K3 is 100), and lightweight models go as low as ~3 — "APIs are expensive" is outdated.

q: True or false: in the 2026 Chinese API market, the same model can cost about half as much for batch jobs at night versus peak daytime hours.
options: True: vendors like DeepSeek use peak/off-peak pricing, off-peak being about half of peak
False: APIs cost the same around the clock
explain: DeepSeek defines peak (weekdays 9:00–12:00, 14:00–18:00) and off-peak windows with a 2× gap; moving batch work off-peak plus using cache is the fastest cost cut — estimate it at reflex-hub.com/en/cost.

q: Which of these is least reliable for a 2026 large model?
options: Translating a paragraph of Chinese into English
Writing a polite complaint email
Multi-digit multiplication and division with a guaranteed zero error rate
Summarizing the central idea of a paper
explain: Language is its strength; pure arithmetic can produce plausible-looking wrong answers — use a calculator or code for that, and let AI call the tools.

q: True or false: the more reference material you give AI, the more accurate its answer necessarily becomes.
options: True: feed it enough and the answer is naturally right
False: too much material drowns the point
explain: Overstuffing buries the key points — models attend least to the middle of long context ("lost in the middle"), and irrelevant material skews the answer; precise beats plentiful.

q: Which Chinese large model, among the highest daily token volumes in 2026, is also deeply integrated into car cockpits?
options: ERNIE Bot (Baidu)
Doubao (ByteDance)
Siri (Apple)
Tmall Genie
explain: Doubao surpassed 180 trillion daily tokens by June, and on Sep 17 its cockpit assistant launched, running in 7+ million vehicles.

q: In 2026, which best describes how Chinese AI companies source training/inference compute?
options: All NVIDIA, no alternative
Already 100% domestic chips
Mainly CPU training
A mix of NVIDIA and domestic chips (Ascend, Cambricon, etc.), with the domestic share rising
explain: Under export controls, "mixed + self-developed" is the norm — Ascend 960 is official and ByteDance and others push self-designed chips, but the NVIDIA installed base is still the mainstay; "all on one side" is never the full story.

q: To get AI to draft your weekly report, which approach yields the most usable output?
options: Just say "write my weekly report"
List the 3 things you did as raw facts and attach your company's report format for it to organize
Let it imagine what you did this week
Run 5 AIs in parallel and vote
explain: AI has writing skill but not your facts — you supply the facts and the format, it supplies the structure. A one-line handoff question only earns correct nonsense.

q: For "the latest" information (today's news, current prices), the most reliable approach is?
options: Ask directly — it knows everything
A pricier model will definitely know
Use a web-search / RAG mode and ask for sources
Repeat the question 10 times for weight
explain: Model knowledge has a training cutoff; "new" information must come from retrieval. Treat an unsourced "latest" answer as fiction by default.

q: You get a voice call from your "daughter" asking to borrow money for an emergency, and the voice sounds exactly right. What is the first step?
options: Wire the money first — family matters
Chat about family trivia to confirm on the call
Forward the recording to friends for help
Hang up, call back on the number you have saved or verify via video / a shared codeword
explain: AI voice cloning works from 3 seconds of sample — "sounds like her" is no longer proof of identity; hanging up and calling back on a number you saved is the only reliable verification.

q: What is the biggest risk of pasting your company's unreleased contract into a public AI assistant?
options: Slow answers
Sensitive information may be retained or used for training, causing a leak
AI will sign contracts for the company
No risk — it's all encrypted
explain: Public AI services have widely differing data policies; pasting unredacted contract or customer data may take it out of your control. Use private deployment or no-retention contracted services for sensitive work, or redact first.
